subject: Information Theory
title: Entropy of a Fair Die
description: A micro-lesson that makes Entropy of a Fair Die usable.

hook.text: A six-sided die has entropy of about 2.58 bits. Why not a round number?

buildup.text: Each face has probability 1/6. Self-information per face: log₂(6) ≈ 2.585 bits.

discovery.text: Since all faces are equally likely, the average equals each individual value. That's the maximum for six outcomes.

twist.text: If one face were more likely, entropy would drop. Bias always reduces uncertainty.

climax.text: 2.58 bits means you need about 2.6 yes-or-no questions on average to identify the result.

punchline.text: Six faces, 2.58 bits. Not round, but exact.

quiz.question: What is the entropy of a fair six-sided die?
